title: DocumentReleaseComment
description: One selected comment, carried as a text body under the document body's capture, representation, structure, segment, excluded-range, and evidence rules unchanged — one text pipeline, three kinds. DocSpec does not select comments: the sealed upstream policy does, and the interface contract is POST-selection rows. Each row projects that policy verbatim so the release cannot disagree with the selection it inherits. The inheritance is the REFUSAL, not the ordering: handed two observations of one comment id the build fails, because resolving a tie would be DocSpec deciding a selection the source owner refused to decide.

commentId.description: EQUALS the catalog's comment `sourceRecordId`, i.e. `/data/id` — the value the upstream selection policy groups by. Minting a second name here would let the release disagree with the selection it inherits.

textBodyId.description: The text body this row belongs to, EQUAL to its own `commentId` — one body per comment, and a second name would be a second identity for one thing.

textKind.description: Which kind of text body this row belongs to. Exactly TEXT_SOURCE_KINDS minus `metadata-field`: one text pipeline, three kinds.

documentId.description: The one document this comment was filed against. A comment's owner is exactly one document and may itself own attachments, so the ownership graph is two levels deep and acyclic.

sourceItemId.description: The member of the requested universe U this comment was selected into. Comments reach a release only where the pinned catalog selects them into U; the zero-accepted-failure bijection then binds them exactly as it binds document bodies.

sourceIssuedVersion.description: The version the SOURCE issued, projected unchanged from the catalog. Never a capture digest.

excludedRanges.description: Representation ranges deliberately not searchable, each with a reason. Every representation byte must be covered by a search segment or by exactly one of these.

commentSelection.description: The sealed upstream selection policy, projected verbatim, plus its digest and the normalized instant the selected observation was ordered on. Every field here is READ from the source owner; none is decided by this release. The three policy fields are constants because there is exactly one sealed policy: a row declaring another policy would be a release claiming a selection nobody sealed.

tieDisposition.description: The refusal this release inherits. Handed two observations of one comment id whose normalized instants are equal, the build fails; it does not re-order, tie-break, or pick the first.

policyDigest.description: The sealed selection policy's own digest, projected verbatim from the source. DocSpec does not compute it: DocSpec does not select comments, so a digest minted here would be a second, weaker report of a fact the source owner already sealed.

selectedModifyDate.description: The normalized `modifyDate` of the observation the policy selected, or null where the source published none — which is exactly what `NULLS LAST` in the ordering exists to place.

captureRecord.description: Links the captured bytes to the exact catalog snapshot, source item, source-issued version, and candidate rendition. Under amendment B1 a `/3` set digest DOES frame this record -- its digests and byte sizes are logical facts about the corpus, and leaving them out is what let a same-length mutation of a body keep its release's name. Exactly two fields stay out of every preimage: `objectKey`, which says where a byte landed and would make a repack a new release, and the acquisition wall clock, which would make two byte-identical captures two releases (deviation row 10). The clock stays in the RECORD, because the provenance a reader needs survives there.

catalogReleaseId.description: The pinned `SourceCatalog` snapshot's own `catalogId`. Same pattern as the root pin's `catalogId`, and checked against it: fixing one and not the other would make every capture row disagree with the root.

objectKey.description: Relative POSIX path of the immutable, digest-pinned member holding the exact captured bytes.

expectedSha256.description: The digest the catalog declared before capture, when it knew one. Non-null means it MUST equal `sha256`; the build fails otherwise.

acquiredAt.description: When the captured bytes were acquired, mirroring `CapturedFile.acquired_at`. Required: erasing acquisition time would destroy provenance the reader needs.

acquisitionStartedAt.description: When the acquisition attempt began, mirroring `CapturedFile.acquisition_started_at`, or null when the downloader reported no start. Written, never omitted.

representation.description: The one selected human-readable Unicode representation. Markup is not search text: this is visible text extracted before segmentation, and every offset in this release counts its UTF-8 bytes.
